claim: IgM emerged in jawed vertebrates 500 million years ago (Mya).
source: IgM emerged in jawed vertebrates 500 Mya and remains the most evolutionarily conserved antibody class.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: IgM is the most evolutionarily conserved antibody class.
source: IgM emerged in jawed vertebrates 500 Mya and remains the most evolutionarily conserved antibody class.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract supported by evolutionary analysis throughout the manuscript.

claim: Significant virus-specific sIgM titers are generated in the serum and gut mucus of largemouth bass that survive LMBV infection.
source: Here, significant virus-specific sIgM titers are generated in the serum and gut mucus of a teleost fish (largemouth bass) that survive infection, and fish lacking sIgM were more susceptible to viral infection.
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data showing LMBV-specific IgM titers in serum and gut mucus of survivor fish (Figure 3L and M).

claim: Fish lacking sIgM are more susceptible to viral infection.
source: Here, significant virus-specific sIgM titers are generated in the serum and gut mucus of a teleost fish (largemouth bass) that survive infection, and fish lacking sIgM were more susceptible to viral infection.
evidence: This is demonstrated by IgM depletion experiments showing increased mortality and viral loads in IgM-depleted fish (Figure 5).

claim: The paradigm that IgM and IgT are specialized to systemic and mucosal immunity, respectively, is challenged by these results.
source: These results challenge the paradigm that IgM and IgT are specialized to systemic and mucosal immunity, respectively.
evidence: This is based on the finding of significant IgM responses in both systemic and mucosal compartments.

claim: Teleost sIgM blocks viral infection by directly targeting viral particles.
source: More crucially, the neutralization assay provides further insight into the role of sIgM in viral neutralization and clarifies the mechanism through which teleost sIgM blocks viral infection by directly targeting viral particles.
evidence: This is supported by time-of-addition assays showing that sIgM inhibits viral infection when applied to viruses before and during adsorption (Figure 7).

claim: sIgM in both primitive and modern vertebrates follows conserved principles in the development of specialized antiviral immunity.
source: From an evolutionary perspective, sIgM in both primitive and modern vertebrates follows conserved principles in the development of specialized antiviral immunity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of teleost IgM function with mammalian IgM function described throughout the manuscript.

claim: The origin of immunoglobulins in jawed vertebrates can be traced back approximately 500 million years ago.
source: The origin of immunoglobulins (Ig) in jawed vertebrates can be traced back approximately 500 million years ago (Mya), marking a significant milestone in the evolution of the adaptive immune system in vertebrates (Parra et al., 2013; Hirano et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Parra et al., 2013 and Hirano et al., 2011.

claim: All jawed vertebrates express multiple classes of Igs.
source: All jawed vertebrates, including mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, bony fish, and cartilaginous fish, express multiple classes of Igs (Parra et al., 2013; Stavnezer and Amemiya, 2004; Han et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Parra et al., 2013; Stavnezer and Amemiya, 2004; Han et al., 2016.

claim: Agnathans do not possess bona fide Ig but have variable lymphocyte receptors (VLRs) capable of mediating adaptive immune responses.
source: Agnathans, the most ancient vertebrate lineage, do not possess bona fide Ig but have variable lymphocyte receptors (VLRs) capable of mediating adaptive immune responses (Flajnik, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Flajnik, 2018.

claim: Cartilaginous fish are the earliest vertebrates to have evolved an adaptive immune system based on Igs.
source: Cartilaginous fish are the earliest vertebrates, from a phylogenetic perspective, to have evolved an adaptive immune system based on Igs.
evidence: This is a statement based on phylogenetic knowledge.

claim: Three Ig isotypes have been identified in Chondrichthyes: IgM, IgW, and IgNAR.
source: To date, three Ig isotypes have been identified in Chondrichthyes: IgM, IgW (which is homologous to IgD; Xu et al., 2016; Edholm et al., 2010), and IgNAR (a lineage-specific isotype unique to cartilaginous fish; Dooley, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Xu et al., 2016; Edholm et al., 2010; and Dooley, 2018.

claim: IgW is homologous to IgD.
source: To date, three Ig isotypes have been identified in Chondrichthyes: IgM, IgW (which is homologous to IgD; Xu et al., 2016; Edholm et al., 2010), and IgNAR (a lineage-specific isotype unique to cartilaginous fish; Dooley, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Xu et al., 2016 and Edholm et al., 2010.

claim: IgNAR is a lineage-specific isotype unique to cartilaginous fish.
source: To date, three Ig isotypes have been identified in Chondrichthyes: IgM, IgW (which is homologous to IgD; Xu et al., 2016; Edholm et al., 2010), and IgNAR (a lineage-specific isotype unique to cartilaginous fish; Dooley, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Dooley, 2018.

claim: IgT is exclusively expressed in teleost fish and represents the most primitive Ig isotype specialized in mucosal immune response.
source: IgT is exclusively expressed in teleost fish and represents the most primitive Ig isotype specialized in mucosal immune response (Zhang et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2010.

claim: IgT is absent in some teleost species including medaka, channel catfish, Atlantic cod, and turquoise killifish.
source: Notably, while IgT has been identified in the majority of teleost species, genomic analyses reveal its absence in some species, such as medaka (Oryzias latipes), channel catfish (Ictalurus punctatus), Atlantic cod (Gadus morhua), and turquoise killifish (Nothobranchius furzeri; Bengtén et al., 2002; Bradshaw and Valenzano, 2020; Magadán-Mompó et al., 2011; Györkei et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bengtén et al., 2002; Bradshaw and Valenzano, 2020; Magadán-Mompó et al., 2011; Györkei et al., 2024.

claim: Avian and mammalian IgA evolved from a precursor of amphibian IgX.
source: The prevailing perspective is that avian and mammalian IgA evolved from a precursor of amphibian IgX, whereas mammalian IgG and IgE evolved from a precursor of amphibian IgY (Schaerlinger et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schaerlinger et al., 2008.

claim: Mammalian IgG and IgE evolved from a precursor of amphibian IgY.
source: The prevailing perspective is that avian and mammalian IgA evolved from a precursor of amphibian IgX, whereas mammalian IgG and IgE evolved from a precursor of amphibian IgY (Schaerlinger et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schaerlinger et al., 2008.

claim: The discovery of IgD in an ostrich species confirmed its presence across all classes of jawed vertebrates.
source: However, the discovery of IgD in an ostrich species (Struthio camelus) confirmed its presence across all classes of jawed vertebrates, fundamentally reshaping our understanding of Ig isotype evolution (Flajnik and Kasahara, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Flajnik and Kasahara, 2010.

claim: IgM is present in all extant gnathostomes, with the potential unique exception of the coelacanth.
source: Similar to IgD, IgM is considered one of the most primordial Ig isotypes throughout evolution, as it is present in all extant gnathostomes, with the potential unique exception of the coelacanth (Keyt et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Keyt et al., 2020.

claim: IgM's ability to form polymeric structures is particularly suited for binding to viral surface proteins.
source: Compared to other Ig isotypes, an exceptionally conserved feature of IgM is its ability to form polymeric structures, which are particularly suited for binding to viral surface proteins (Boes, 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Boes, 2000.

claim: In cartilaginous fishes and tetrapods, IgM is secreted as a J chain-linked pentamer.
source: In cartilaginous fishes and tetrapods, IgM is secreted as a J chain-linked pentamer, which may enhance multivalent antigen recognition (Hagiwara et al., 1985; Hohman et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hagiwara et al., 1985 and Hohman et al., 2003.

claim: Teleosts have undergone J chain gene loss, resulting in the stable formation of tetrameric IgM.
source: By contrast, teleosts have undergone J chain gene loss, resulting in the stable formation of tetrameric IgM (Bromage et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bromage et al., 2004.

claim: IgM is the largest Ig class in plasma and the first antibody produced during an antiviral humoral response.
source: It is the largest Ig classes in plasma and the first antibody produced during an antiviral humoral response (Schroeder and Cavacini, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schroeder and Cavacini, 2010.

claim: IgM is generally considered to be a major Ig isotype that plays a key role in the antiviral systemic immune response.
source: Although previous studies have suggested that IgM is involved in maintaining mucosal tissue homeostasis, it is generally considered to be a major Ig isotype that plays a key role in the antiviral systemic immune response (Ochsenbein et al., 1999; Boes et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ochsenbein et al., 1999 and Boes et al., 1998.

claim: IgM may contribute to mucosal protection during the early stages of life.
source: Indeed, IgM serves not only as a crucial effector molecule in the initial humoral defense against pathogens but may also contribute to mucosal protection during the early stages of life (Chen et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Chen et al., 2020.

claim: IgM is rapidly produced early in the humoral immune response against viral infections, providing fast and strong protective immunity.
source: According to commonly held views, IgM is rapidly produced early in the humoral immune response against viral infections, providing fast and strong protective immunity (Ouchida et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ouchida et al., 2012.

claim: For certain viruses such as polyomavirus and vesicular stomatitis virus, IgM provides sufficient protection against fatal infection during the acute phase.
source: For certain viruses predominantly controlled by B cells, such as polyomavirus and vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV), IgM provides sufficient protection against fatal infection during the acute phase (Beebe and Cooper, 1981; Nguyen et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Beebe and Cooper, 1981 and Nguyen et al., 2023.

claim: Long-lived, antigen-specific IgM plasma cells exist in mice.
source: However, recent studies in mice revealed the presence of long-lived, antigen-specific IgM plasma cells (Bohannon et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bohannon et al., 2016.

claim: Neutralizing antibodies secreted by plasma cells are the fundamental molecular armament of antiviral humoral immunity.
source: Neutralizing antibodies (NAbs) secreted by plasma cells are the fundamental molecular armament of antiviral humoral immunity, serving as the primary mechanism through which Igs protect the body from viral infection (Ali et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ali et al., 2020.

claim: Plasma from SARS-CoV-2 convalescent individuals exhibits IgM-mediated neutralization activity, with neutralization titers showing a strong correlation with IgM levels.
source: New research on SARS-CoV-2 provides compelling evidence that plasma from convalescent individuals also exhibits IgM-mediated neutralization activity, with neutralization titers showing a strong correlation with IgM levels (Ku et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ku et al., 2021.

claim: IgM is the predominant Ig isotype involved in the immune response to pathogens in systemic compartments of teleost fish.
source: Recent studies have demonstrated that IgM is the predominant Ig isotype involved in the immune response to pathogens in systemic compartments (e.g. serum, spleen, and head kidney), where significant accumulations of IgM+ B cells were found after infection with parasitic and bacterial pathogens (Xu et al., 2016; Xu et al., 2013; Yu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Xu et al., 2016; Xu et al., 2013; Yu et al., 2018.

claim: The serum of fish that survive parasitic or bacterial infection harbors high levels of pathogen-specific IgM, coupled with negligible IgT-specific titers and no specific IgD.
source: Notably, the serum of fish that survive parasitic or bacterial infection harbors high levels of pathogen-specific IgM, coupled with negligible IgT-specific titers and no specific IgD.
evidence: This is a statement based on previous research findings.

claim: IgT is the main Ig response in the mucus of fish infected with parasites or bacteria.
source: In contrast, IgT is the main Ig response in the mucus of the same fish.
evidence: This is a statement based on previous research findings.

claim: Induced viral-specific sIgT within the mucus is capable of neutralizing viruses.
source: Additionally, previous studies reported that induced viral-specific sIgT within the mucus is capable of neutralizing viruses, with fish lacking IgT being significantly more susceptible to viruses compared to those with IgT, suggesting that sIgT is essential for the control of mucosal pathogens (Yu et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yu et al., 2022.

claim: Fish lacking IgT are significantly more susceptible to viruses compared to those with IgT.
source: Additionally, previous studies reported that induced viral-specific sIgT within the mucus is capable of neutralizing viruses, with fish lacking IgT being significantly more susceptible to viruses compared to those with IgT, suggesting that sIgT is essential for the control of mucosal pathogens (Yu et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yu et al., 2022.

claim: Specific IgM levels were significantly increased in both serum and gut mucus upon Aeromonas hydrophila and SVCV infection.
source: Interestingly, recent observations show that specific IgM levels were significantly increased in both serum and gut mucus upon Aeromonas hydrophila and spring viremia of carp (SVCV) infection, challenging the paradigm that pathogen-specific IgT and IgM responses are strictly compartmentalized in mucosal and systemic immunity, respectively (Mu et al., 2022; Yu et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Mu et al., 2022 and Yu et al., 2024.

claim: Teleost fish can produce specific serum and mucus sIgM recognizing viral antigens in response to viruses across a wide range of teleost species.
source: Previous studies have demonstrated the capacity of teleost fish to produce specific serum and mucus sIgM recognizing viral antigens in response to viruses across a wide range of teleost species (Mashoof and Criscitiello, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mashoof and Criscitiello, 2016.

claim: LMBV infection induces typical symptoms and severe pathological changes in largemouth bass.
source: To verify the aforementioned hypothesis, a viral infection model was established by intraperitoneally injecting largemouth bass (Micropterus salmoides) with largemouth bass virus (LMBV), which induces typical symptoms and severe pathological changes, evoking a robust immune response in both systemic and mucosal areas.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing symptoms, pathology, and immune responses (Figure 1).

claim: LMBV infection evokes a robust immune response in both systemic and mucosal areas of largemouth bass.
source: To verify the aforementioned hypothesis, a viral infection model was established by intraperitoneally injecting largemouth bass (Micropterus salmoides) with largemouth bass virus (LMBV), which induces typical symptoms and severe pathological changes, evoking a robust immune response in both systemic and mucosal areas.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing immune gene expression and immune cell responses (Figures 2 and 3).

claim: LMBV infection results in significant proliferation and accumulation of IgM+ B cells in the gut and head kidney.
source: The data revealed significant proliferation and accumulation of IgM+ B cells in the gut and head kidney, accompanied by increased viral-specific sIgM titers in serum and mucus, reinforcing the notion that sIgM participates in both mucosal and systemic immunity.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence and flow cytometry data (Figure 3).

claim: LMBV infection is accompanied by increased viral-specific sIgM titers in serum and mucus.
source: The data revealed significant proliferation and accumulation of IgM+ B cells in the gut and head kidney, accompanied by increased viral-specific sIgM titers in serum and mucus, reinforcing the notion that sIgM participates in both mucosal and systemic immunity.
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data (Figure 3L and M).

claim: Fish devoid of sIgM are more susceptible to LMBV than control fish.
source: To further validate the role of sIgM in antiviral defense, an IgM depletion model was employed in teleost fish, revealing that fish devoid of sIgM are more susceptible to the virus than control fish.
evidence: This is supported by mortality and viral load data from IgM depletion experiments (Figure 5).

claim: Induced virus-specific sIgM can neutralize viruses in vitro.
source: Importantly, the induced virus-specific sIgM can neutralize viruses in vitro, thereby revealing an effector role of sIgM in both serum and gut mucus against viral infection.
evidence: This is supported by neutralization assay data (Figure 6).

claim: IgM serves as an ancient weapon in the adaptive immune response against viral infections, preserved throughout evolution across all vertebrates.
source: Collectively, these data provide proof of concept that IgM serves as an ancient weapon in the adaptive immune response against viral infections, preserved throughout evolution across all vertebrates.
evidence: This is an inference based on the functional conservation of IgM observed in teleosts and mammals.

claim: Infected largemouth bass exhibited typical symptoms such as skin ulceration, subdermal hemorrhage, and spleen enlargement at 4 DPI.
source: The infected fish exhibited typical symptoms, such as skin ulceration, subdermal hemorrhage, and spleen enlargement, at 4 DPI (Figure 1B–D), reaching a cumulative mortality of 57% within 14 days (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is directly observed and documented in Figure 1B-D.

claim: LMBV-infected largemouth bass reached a cumulative mortality of 57% within 14 days.
source: The infected fish exhibited typical symptoms, such as skin ulceration, subdermal hemorrhage, and spleen enlargement, at 4 DPI (Figure 1B–D), reaching a cumulative mortality of 57% within 14 days (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is shown in the survival curve in Figure 1E.

claim: High LMBV loads were present in the spleen, head kidney, and gut, especially at 4 DPI.
source: qPCR analyses revealed the presence of high LMBV loads in the spleen (SP), head kidney (HK), and gut, especially at 4 DPI (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is shown by qPCR data in Figure 1F.

claim: LMBV was present in the SP, HK, and gut of infected fish at 4 DPI as shown by immunofluorescence microscopy.
source: Immunofluorescence microscopy studies using an anti-LMBV-MCP monoclonal antibody (mAb) indicated that the virus was present in the SP, HK, and gut of the infected fish at 4 DPI (Figure 1G, with isotype-matched control antibodies shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence images in Figure 1G.

claim: TEM images showed the accumulation of numerous LMBV particles in the HK, SP, and gut.
source: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images also showed the accumulation of numerous LMBV particles in the HK, SP, and gut (Figure 1H), indicating successful viral invasion of these tissues.
evidence: This is shown by TEM images in Figure 1H.

claim: The homogenate supernatant from SP, HK, or gut of infected fish at 4 DPI resulted in a notable cytopathic effect in cell cultures.
source: Importantly, the homogenate supernatant from SP, HK, or gut of infected fish at 4 DPI resulted in a notable cytopathic effect (CPE) in cell cultures (Figure 1I).
evidence: This is shown by CPE images in Figure 1I.

claim: Largemouth bass occurred with varying degrees of cytoplasmic lesions at 4 DPI, including HK and SP cellular necrosis, intestinal epithelial cell shedding, and erythrocyte infiltration.
source: Moreover, histological analysis revealed that largemouth bass occurred with varying degrees of cytoplasmic lesions at 4 DPI, including HK and SP cellular necrosis, intestinal epithelial cell shedding, and erythrocyte infiltration (Figure 1J).
evidence: This is shown by histological images in Figure 1J.

claim: Upon viral infection, inflammation, innate, and adaptive immune responses were triggered in the HK, SP, and gut tissues.
source: qPCR results indicated that upon viral infection, inflammation, innate, and adaptive immune responses were triggered in the HK, SP, and gut tissues (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is shown by qPCR heatmaps in Figure 2A-C.

claim: The innate and adaptive immune responses were most intense at 4 and 28 DPI, respectively.
source: The innate and adaptive immune responses were most intense at 4 and 28 DPI, respectively.
evidence: This is inferred from the qPCR and RNA-Seq data showing peak expression of innate genes at 4 DPI and adaptive genes at 28 DPI.

claim: 1237 and 1388 genes were up-regulated in the HK at 4 and 28 DPI, respectively.
source: Specifically, 1237 and 1388 genes were up-regulated in the HK at 4 and 28 DPI, whereas 22 and 1413 genes were up-regulated in the gut at these time points.
evidence: This is shown by RNA-Seq analysis results.

claim: 22 and 1413 genes were up-regulated in the gut at 4 and 28 DPI, respectively.
source: Specifically, 1237 and 1388 genes were up-regulated in the HK at 4 and 28 DPI, whereas 22 and 1413 genes were up-regulated in the gut at these time points.
evidence: This is shown by RNA-Seq analysis results.

claim: 1616 and 916 genes were down-regulated in the HK at 4 and 28 DPI, respectively.
source: Additionally, 1616 and 916 genes were down-regulated in the HK, and 2004 and 143 extensive changes in immune-related genes in the HK and gut at 4 and 28 DPI (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This is shown by RNA-Seq analysis results.

claim: GO and KEGG analyses indicated an antiviral immune response process occurring in the HK and gut, with enrichment in pathways such as NF-kappa B signaling, Epstein-Barr virus infection, and the intestinal immune network for IgA production.
source: Subsequent Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analyses of these differentially expressed genes (DEGs) indicated an antiviral immune response process occurring in the HK and gut, with enrichment in pathways such as NF-kappa B signaling, Epstein-Barr virus infection, and the intestinal immune network for IgA production (Figure 2F and G).
evidence: This is shown by GO and KEGG enrichment analyses in Figure 2F and G.

claim: Key genes involved in antiviral responses and innate immunity were up-regulated at 4 DPI in both HK and gut tissues.
source: Furthermore, key genes involved in antiviral responses and innate immunity were up-regulated at 4 DPI, whereas genes associated with adaptive immunity were up-regulated at 28 DPI in both HK and gut tissues (Figure 2H and I).
evidence: This is shown by gene expression heatmaps in Figure 2H and I.

claim: Genes associated with adaptive immunity were up-regulated at 28 DPI in both HK and gut tissues.
source: Furthermore, key genes involved in antiviral responses and innate immunity were up-regulated at 4 DPI, whereas genes associated with adaptive immunity were up-regulated at 28 DPI in both HK and gut tissues (Figure 2H and I).
evidence: This is shown by gene expression heatmaps in Figure 2H and I.

claim: IgM exhibited high expression levels in systemic (HK and SP) and mucosal (gut) tissues of infected fish at 28 DPI.
source: Importantly, IgM exhibited high expression levels in systemic (HK and SP) and mucosal (gut) tissues of infected fish at 28 DPI (Figure 2A–C, H and I), suggesting that IgM plays a role in both systemic and mucosal compartments.
evidence: This is shown by qPCR and RNA-Seq data in Figures 2A-C, H, and I.

claim: A moderate accumulation in IgM+ B cells was observed in the HK and gut of the 28DPI-S fish compared to the control group.
source: Immunofluorescence microscopy analysis revealed a moderate accumulation in IgM+ B cells in the HK and gut of the 28DPI-S fish compared to the control group (Con), with a notable increase observed in the 42DPI-S fish (Figure 3B–E), with isotype-matched control antibodies shown in (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence images and quantification in Figure 3B-E.

claim: A notable increase in IgM+ B cells was observed in the 42DPI-S fish.
source: Immunofluorescence microscopy analysis revealed a moderate accumulation in IgM+ B cells in the HK and gut of the 28DPI-S fish compared to the control group (Con), with a notable increase observed in the 42DPI-S fish (Figure 3B–E), with isotype-matched control antibodies shown in (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence images and quantification in Figure 3B-E.

claim: A significant increase in the number of EdU+ IgM+ B cells was observed in both the HK and gut of the 28DPI-S fish compared to controls.
source: Flow cytometry analysis revealed a significant increase in the number of EdU+ IgM+ B cells in both the HK and gut of the 28DPI-S fish compared to controls, with more pronounced proliferation observed in the 42DPI-S fish (Figure 3F–I).
evidence: This is shown by flow cytometry data in Figure 3F-I.

claim: More pronounced proliferation of IgM+ B cells was observed in the 42DPI-S fish.
source: Flow cytometry analysis revealed a significant increase in the number of EdU+ IgM+ B cells in both the HK and gut of the 28DPI-S fish compared to controls, with more pronounced proliferation observed in the 42DPI-S fish (Figure 3F–I).
evidence: This is shown by flow cytometry data in Figure 3F-I.

claim: sIgM protein levels in the serum of 28DPI-S and 42DPI-S fish increased by approximately 2.3- and 3.9-fold compared to control fish, respectively.
source: Along with the increases in IgM+ B cells, sIgM protein levels in the serum of 28DPI-S and 42DPI-S fish increased by approximately 2.3- and 3.9-fold compared to control fish, respectively (Figure 3J).
evidence: This is shown by western blot quantification in Figure 3J.

claim: In the gut mucus, the IgM concentration increased by approximately 1.6- and 3.8-fold in 28DPI-S and 42DPI-S fish, respectively.
source: In the gut mucus, the IgM concentration increased by approximately 1.6- and 3.8-fold in 28DPI-S and 42DPI-S fish, respectively (Figure 3K).
evidence: This is shown by western blot quantification in Figure 3K.

claim: Fish in the 42DPI-S group exhibited higher LMBV-specific IgM titers in both serum (~36,267) and gut (~230) compared to those in the serum (~7867) and gut (~41) of fish in the 28DPI-S group.
source: Consistent with the sIgM protein expression levels, fish in the 42DPI-S group exhibited higher LMBV-specific IgM titers in both serum (~36,267) and gut (~230) compared to those in the serum (~7867) and gut (~41) of fish in the 28DPI-S group (Figure 3L and M).
evidence: This is shown by ELISA data in Figure 3L and M.

claim: Approximately 57% of the fish in the control-challenge (CC) group died following LMBV challenge.
source: Following the challenge, approximately 57% of the fish in the control-challenge (CC) group died, whereas only 10% of the fish in the 42DPI-S challenge (SC) group died (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is shown by survival curve data in Figure 4B.

claim: Only 10% of the fish in the 42DPI-S challenge (SC) group died following LMBV challenge.
source: Following the challenge, approximately 57% of the fish in the control-challenge (CC) group died, whereas only 10% of the fish in the 42DPI-S challenge (SC) group died (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is shown by survival curve data in Figure 4B.

claim: Viral loads in the HK and gut were significantly lower in the SC group compared to the CC group.
source: qPCR analyses revealed that viral loads in the HK and gut were significantly lower in the SC group compared to the CC group (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: This is shown by qPCR data in Figure 4C and D.

claim: High viral loads were present in the HK and gut of the CC group, whereas very low viral loads were detected in the 42DPI-SC group.
source: Immunofluorescence microscopy further confirmed that high viral loads were present in the HK (Figure 4E and F) and gut (Figure 4G and H) of the CC group, whereas very low viral loads were detected in the 42DPI-SC group (Figure 4E–H).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence images and quantification in Figure 4E-H.

claim: Significant histological damage was observed in the HK and gut of CC fish compared to control fish.
source: Pathological examination showed significant histological damage in the HK and gut of CC fish compared to control fish (Figure 4I–L).
evidence: This is shown by histological images and pathology scores in Figure 4I-L.

claim: No visible tissue damage was observed in either the 42DPI-S or 42DPI-SC groups.
source: Interestingly, no visible tissue damage was observed in either the 42DPI-S or 42DPI-SC groups (Figure 4I–L).
evidence: This is shown by histological images and pathology scores in Figure 4I-L.

claim: IgM+ B cells were significantly depleted in blood (49.7–98.9%), SP (42.7–89.8%), and gut (50.1–88.3%) from day 1 to day 7 post-depletion.
source: Flow cytometry analysis revealed that IgM+ B cells were significantly depleted in blood (49.7–98.9%), SP (42.7–89.8%), and gut (50.1–88.3%) from day 1 to day 7 post-depletion, with the most substantial depletion observed at day 3 compared to control fish (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–F).
evidence: This is shown by flow cytometry data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-F.

claim: The depletion of IgM+ B cells led to significant reductions in IgM protein levels in serum (49.7%–96.6%) and gut mucus (69.5%–90.1%) until day 10 post-depletion.
source: Moreover, the depletion of IgM+ B cells also led to significant reductions in IgM protein levels in serum (49.7%–96.6%) and gut mucus (69.5%–90.1%) until day 10 post-depletion (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A-D).
evidence: This is shown by western blot data in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A-D.

claim: LMBV-specific IgM titers were significantly lower in the IgM+ B cell-depleted 42DPI-S fish compared to the non-depleted group.
source: As anticipated, LMBV-specific IgM titers were significantly lower in the IgM+ B cell-depleted 42DPI-S fish compared to the non-depleted group (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This is shown by ELISA data in Figure 5B and C.

claim: Pronounced histopathological changes were observed in the HK, SP, and gut of IgM+ B cell-depleted 42DPI-S fish compared to the non-depleted group.
source: Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining revealed pronounced histopathological changes in the HK, SP, and gut of IgM+ B cell-depleted 42DPI-S fish compared to the non-depleted group (Figure 5D and E).
evidence: This is shown by histological images and scores in Figure 5D and E.

claim: Elevated levels of LMBV-MCP expression were observed in the tissues of IgM+ B cell-depleted 42DPI-S fish.
source: Moreover, immunofluorescence microscopy and qPCR further confirmed elevated levels of LMBV-MCP expression in the tissues of IgM+ B cell-depleted 42DPI-S fish (Figure 5F–J).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence and qPCR data in Figure 5F-J.

claim: The IgM+ B cell-depleted 42DPI-S group exhibited significantly higher cumulative mortality compared to the non-depleted group.
source: Importantly, the IgM+ B cell-depleted 42DPI-S group exhibited significantly higher cumulative mortality compared to the non-depleted group (Figure 5K).
evidence: This is shown by survival curve data in Figure 5K.

claim: Lower EPC viability and significantly higher CPE were observed in the control and 42DPI-S-IgMDEP groups compared to the 42DPI-S group.
source: Lower EPC viability and significantly higher CPE were observed in the control and 42DPI-S-IgMDEP groups compared to the 42DPI-S group, regardless of whether the sample was derived from serum (Figure 6B and D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A) or gut mucus (Figure 6C and D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that the protective efficacy of 42DPI-S was attributable to LMBV-specific IgM.
evidence: This is shown by cell viability assays and CPE images in Figure 6B-D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: The expression of the LMBV-MCP gene and protein levels were notably decreased in EPC cells treated with the 42DPI-S serum or gut mucus compared to control fish.
source: Consistent with these findings, the expression of the LMBV-MCP gene and protein levels were notably decreased in EPC cells treated with the 42DPI-S serum (Figure 6E, G and I) or gut mucus (Figure 6F, H and J) compared to control fish.
evidence: This is shown by qPCR and western blot data in Figure 6E-J.

claim: LMBV-MCP levels were similar to control fish when IgM was depleted in the 42DPI-S samples.
source: However, their levels were similar to control fish when IgM was depleted in the 42DPI-S samples (Figure 6E–J).
evidence: This is shown by qPCR and western blot data in Figure 6E-J.

claim: The number of LMBV-infected EPC cells treated with 42DPI-S samples decreased significantly compared to the control fish.
source: Similarly, immunofluorescence analysis demonstrated that the number of LMBV-infected EPC cells treated with 42DPI-S samples (i.e. serum and gut mucus) decreased significantly compared to the control fish, whereas the number of infected EPC cells in the 42DPI-S-IgMDEP group increased and nearly returned to the level observed in control fish (Figure 6K–N).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence images and quantification in Figure 6K-N.

claim: A significant reduction in both LMBV-MCP gene expression and protein levels was observed in EPC cells treated with purified IgM from serum or gut mucus.
source: A significant reduction in both LMBV-MCP gene expression and protein levels was observed in EPC cells treated with purified IgM from serum (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A, C and D) or gut mucus (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B, E and F).
evidence: This is shown by qPCR and western blot data in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A-F.

claim: LMBV proliferation levels were significantly inhibited when serum or gut mucus from 42DPI-S fish were applied to viruses throughout the experiment (group 2, G2) or prior to and during adsorption (group 5, G5).
source: In contrast, LMBV proliferation levels were significantly inhibited when serum or gut mucus from 42DPI-S fish were applied to viruses throughout the experiment (group 2, G2) or prior to and during adsorption (group 5, G5; Figure 7B–G).
evidence: This is shown by time-of-addition assay data in Figure 7B-G.

claim: The 42DPI-S-IgMDEP serum or gut mucus no longer exhibited an inhibitory effect on the virus.
source: It is worth mentioning that the 42DPI-S-IgMDEP serum or gut mucus no longer exhibited an inhibitory effect on the virus (Figure 7B–G).
evidence: This is shown by time-of-addition assay data in Figure 7B-G.

claim: Viral-specific IgM mediates neutralization through mechanisms involving directly acting on LMBV particles, causing them to lose their infectivity.
source: These results suggest that viral-specific IgM mediates neutralization through mechanisms involving directly acting on LMBV particles, causing them to lose their infectivity.
evidence: This is inferred from the time-of-addition assay showing that IgM inhibits infection when applied to viruses before cell contact.

claim: IgM has been shown to neutralize viruses in mammals, such as in plasma from convalescent patients recovering from COVID-19.
source: In mammals, IgM has been shown to neutralize viruses, such as in plasma from convalescent patients recovering from COVID-19 (Harrington et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Harrington et al., 2021.

claim: Depletion of IgM in COVID-19 convalescent plasma resulted in a loss of neutralization against SARS-CoV-2, significantly increasing susceptibility.
source: Depletion of IgM in these cases resulted in a loss of neutralization against SARS-CoV-2, significantly increasing susceptibility (Gasser et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Gasser et al., 2021.

claim: The gut harbored higher LMBV loads compared to the HK and SP.
source: Importantly, qPCR analysis demonstrates that the gut harbored higher LMBV loads compared to the HK and SP, indicating that in viral-infected fish, mucosal tissues mount a robust immune response alongside systemic immune organs.
evidence: This is shown by qPCR data in Figure 1F.

claim: Several immune-related genes are significantly upregulated in teleost fish after infection with viral pathogens such as IHNV and VHSV.
source: Previous studies have shown that several immune-related genes are significantly upregulated in teleost fish after infection with viral pathogens such as infectious hematopoietic necrosis virus (IHNV) (Kong et al., 2024; Huang et al., 2022) and viral hemorrhagic septicemia virus (VHSV; Nuñez-Ortiz et al., 2018; Moore et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kong et al., 2024; Huang et al., 2022; Nuñez-Ortiz et al., 2018; Moore et al., 2017.

claim: LMBV infection significantly upregulates several immune genes in both systemic immune organs (HK and SP) and mucosal tissues (gut) of largemouth bass.
source: Similarly, LMBV infection significantly upregulates several immune genes in both systemic immune organs (HK and SP) and mucosal tissues (gut) of largemouth bass.
evidence: This is shown by qPCR and RNA-Seq data in Figure 2.

claim: Numerous IgM-secreting plasma cells and a dramatic increase in sIgM concentrations have been observed in the bone marrow and serum of mammals after influenza virus infection.
source: Similarly, numerous IgM-secreting plasma cells and a dramatic increase in sIgM concentrations have been observed in the bone marrow and serum of mammals after influenza virus infection (Skountzou et al., 2014; Wu et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Skountzou et al., 2014 and Wu et al., 2022.

claim: Virus-specific IgM production has been well-documented in reptiles, birds, and mammals upon viral infection.
source: Virus-specific IgM production has been well-documented in reptiles, birds, and mammals upon viral infection (Dascalu et al., 2024; Harrington et al., 2021; Harrington et al., 2021; Neul et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Dascalu et al., 2024; Harrington et al., 2021; Neul et al., 2017.

claim: Cartilaginous fish and amphibians can mount specific IgM responses against bacterial pathogens and immune antigens.
source: While current evidence confirms the capacity of cartilaginous fish and amphibians to mount specific IgM responses against bacterial pathogens and immune antigens (Dooley and Flajnik, 2005; Ramsey et al., 2010), the potential for viral induction of analogous IgM-mediated immunity in these species remains unresolved.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Dooley and Flajnik, 2005 and Ramsey et al., 2010.

claim: IgM-/- mice, lacking sIgM, lost their resistance to West Nile virus, even following inoculation with low viral doses.
source: Studies on mammals have shown that IgM-/- mice, lacking sIgM, lost their resistance to West Nile virus, even following inoculation with low viral doses (Diamond et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Diamond et al., 2003.

claim: Specific IgM contributes to viral resistance by neutralizing viruses in endotherms (birds and mammals).
source: Extensive studies in endotherms (birds and mammals) have demonstrated that specific IgM contributes to viral resistance by neutralizing viruses (Baumgarth et al., 2000; Diamond et al., 2003; Ku et al., 2021; Hagan et al., 2016; Singh et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Baumgarth et al., 2000; Diamond et al., 2003; Ku et al., 2021; Hagan et al., 2016; Singh et al., 2022.

claim: Viral infections have been shown to induce neutralizing antibodies in Chinese soft-shelled turtles.
source: Although viral infections have been shown to induce neutralizing antibodies in Chinese soft-shelled turtles (Pelodiscus sinensis' Nie and Lu, 1999), the specific Ig isotypes mediating this response have yet to be elucidated.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Nie and Lu, 1999.

claim: IgM in teleost fish has been shown to possess viral neutralizing activity similar to that observed in endotherms.
source: In teleost fish, IgM has been shown to possess viral neutralizing activity similar to that observed in endotherms (Castro et al., 2013; Ye et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Castro et al., 2013 and Ye et al., 2013.

claim: Secretory IgT (sIgT) in rainbow trout can neutralize viruses, significantly reducing susceptibility to infection.
source: Furthermore, recent work demonstrated that secretory IgT (sIgT) in rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) can neutralize viruses, significantly reducing susceptibility to infection (Yu et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yu et al., 2022.

claim: Polymeric IgM mediates neutralization due to its higher avidity and steric hindrance, inhibiting virus attachment and entry into target cells.
source: Polymeric IgM mediates neutralization due to its higher avidity and steric hindrance, inhibiting virus attachment and entry into target cells with great breadth and potency (Shen et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Shen et al., 2019.

claim: IgM mediates neutralization primarily by targeting the receptor-binding domain (RBD) of viruses, blocking virus binding to cell receptors.
source: A growing body of evidence suggests that IgM mediates neutralization primarily by targeting the receptor-binding domain (RBD) of viruses, blocking virus binding to cell receptors, and effectively preventing infection (Warr et al., 1979; Zhu et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Warr et al., 1979 and Zhu et al., 2023.

claim: IgM antibodies exhibit strong neutralizing activity during viral hemorrhagic septicemia virus (VHSV) infections in trout and zebrafish.
source: These results align with previous findings that IgM antibodies exhibit strong neutralizing activity during viral hemorrhagic septicemia virus (VHSV) infections in trout and zebrafish (Chinchilla et al., 2013; Castro et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chinchilla et al., 2013 and Castro et al., 2021.

claim: The mechanism through which IgM neutralizes viruses may involve the direct destruction of the virus through antibody-imposed structural collisions that damage its integrity.
source: The mechanism through which IgM neutralizes viruses may involve the direct destruction of the virus. This is consistent with recent research suggesting that physical disruption of the virus through antibody-imposed structural collisions damages its integrity, thus reducing its infectivity (Zheng et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zheng et al., 2019.

claim: Virus-specific IgM antibodies in teleost fish constitute a primary line of defense in the systemic humoral response against viral infections, while also providing mucosal protection.
source: Importantly, virus-specific IgM antibodies in teleost fish constitute a primary line of defense in the systemic humoral response against viral infections, while also providing mucosal protection.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data showing IgM responses in both systemic and mucosal compartments.

claim: sIgM holds an important role in both mucosal and systemic immunity.
source: Therefore, these data further support the concept that sIgM holds an important role in both mucosal and systemic immunity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data showing IgM responses in both compartments.

claim: Upon LMBV infection, severe histological changes and robust adaptive immune responses occur in systemic (e.g. HK) and mucosal (gut) tissues.
source: Upon infection, severe histological changes and robust adaptive immune responses occur in systemic (e.g. HK) and mucosal (gut) tissues.
evidence: This is shown by histological and gene expression data in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: IgM+ B cells in the HK and gut were activated, underwent local proliferation, and differentiated into plasma cells to produce virus-specific IgM.
source: Subsequently, IgM+ B cells in the HK and gut were activated, underwent local proliferation, and differentiated into plasma cells to produce virus-specific IgM.
evidence: This is shown by EdU proliferation assays and IgM titer measurements in Figure 3.

claim: Specific IgM possesses the capacity for viral neutralization and can directly act on viral particles to block infection.
source: Crucially, the neutralization assay results indicate that specific IgM possesses the capacity for viral neutralization and can directly act on viral particles to block infection.
evidence: This is shown by neutralization assays in Figures 6 and 7.

claim: sIgM in both primitive and modern vertebrates utilize conserved mechanisms in response to viral infections.
source: Although the definitive mechanisms of teleost sIgM in antiviral defense were not fully characterized in this study, these observations suggest that sIgM in both primitive and modern vertebrates utilize conserved mechanisms in response to viral infections.
evidence: This is an inference based on the functional similarities between teleost and mammalian IgM.

claim: sIgM may contribute to viral resistance in fish mucosal compartments.
source: Finally, these data demonstrated that sIgM may contribute to viral resistance in fish mucosal compartments, which has significant implications for the future design of fish vaccines aimed at enhancing mucosal sIgM responses.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data showing IgM responses in mucosal tissues.

claim: IgM is present across all classes of jawed vertebrates as shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.
source: IgM stands out as the isotype conserved among jawed vertebrates.
evidence: This is illustrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 showing IgM presence across vertebrate classes.
